rationale: The VerifyLeader account's first limitation says that only one suffrage shape was exercised, five members with two non-voters, and that a single non-voter was not tested. This experiment supplies it: four members, one demoted to a non-voter, so the configuration has three voters and exactly one non-voter, and the voter quorum is two. With the leader cut from the two other voters and the single non-voter reachable, the leader can reach only itself among the voters; a verification that succeeds there shows the defect needs one non-voter rather than a particular mix. The control cuts the non-voter as well. A local probe produced the pair, verification succeeding immediately with the non-voter reachable and failing with the message about losing leadership once it was cut.

scope.description: Four real members over the cluster helper's in-memory transports, bootstrapped from one four-voter configuration; one non-leader member is demoted with DemoteVoter and the harness waits until that member's own configuration view no longer lists it as a voter. The leader is then disconnected in both directions from the two other voters and, in the trigger, left connected to the single non-voter; the control also disconnects the non-voter. Each case records the reachable voter and non-voter counts, the voter quorum, whether the demotion converged, and the bounded VerifyLeader result with the node's state afterwards.
assumptions: Bidirectional route removal on the in-memory transports models a partition; no process is stopped.
The demoted member's own view is the check that the configuration change reached the node whose acknowledgement is being counted.
A verification that has not completed within two seconds is recorded as incomplete rather than as a success or failure.
excluded: No client read and no second suffrage shape beyond one non-voter.
No demotion of the sitting leader and no cluster larger than four members.
No variation of the lease timeout.

experiment.prefix: The harness bootstraps four voters, picks the leader and the three other members, demotes the first non-leader member, and polls that member's GetConfiguration until it no longer reports itself as a voter or two seconds pass, recording whether it converged and after how long. It then disconnects the leader's transport from the other two voters' addresses and theirs from the leader's, and in the control case does the same for the non-voter. It emits vx_case_<case> with the membership counts, the reachable counts, the voter quorum and the demotion convergence, calls VerifyLeader with a two-second bound, and emits vx_result_<case> with whether the call completed, whether it succeeded, its error, the elapsed milliseconds and the node's state afterwards.
experiment.responsibility: VerifyLeader sizes its quorum from the voter count, so a leader that can reach only itself among the voters has one of the two acknowledgements its own sizing requires. The experiment asks whether a single non-voter, rather than a particular larger suffrage mix, is enough to supply the missing acknowledgement and let the call report success.
semantic_changes: The cluster has four members and one non-voter instead of five members and two non-voters.
The harness records whether the demoted member's own configuration converged before the partition, so the case cannot be explained by a stale view on the acknowledging node.
Case and result events use a new prefix so they cannot be confused with the earlier five-member receipts.

comparisons.description: With one of three voters reachable, a verification sized on the voter quorum must fail; the harness records whether a single non-voter changes that.
Control: with the non-voter unreachable too, no supporter remains and the verification must fail.
